point: make + object + adjective.
make + 受詞 + 形容詞。
why: The object of makes is the whole phrase the items that customers order most often. The blank says what those items become, so it needs an adjective: accessible.
makes 的受詞是整段 the items that customers order most often。空格說明這些商品變得怎樣，所以要形容詞：accessible。

gloss.ex: We changed the layout of the lobby.
Each picker carries a handheld scanner.
She works the night shift on Fridays.

point: The blank is the subject: use a noun.
空格是主詞：用名詞。
why: The main verb comes late: will be accepted. Everything from the blank to Avenue is the subject. What gets accepted? Applications.
主要動詞出現得很晚：will be accepted。從空格到 Avenue 都是主詞。什麼會被受理？Applications。

gloss.ex: The assistant branch manager signs the daily reports.
Log in to the employee portal to check your pay.

point: An action lasting up to a past time: had been + Ving.
持續到過去某時點的動作：had been + Ving。
why: The sentence ends with when Ms. Ferrante was hired, a moment in the past. Before that moment, the center had run for nearly two years. So the form is had been operating.
句尾 when Ms. Ferrante was hired 是過去的時點。在那之前，客服中心已經運作了 for nearly two years。所以用 had been operating。

gloss.ex: She works at a call center downtown.
Two clerks handle all customer complaints.
The scheduling software saves us hours each week.

point: A finished past time (last quarter): simple past.
已結束的過去時間（last quarter）：過去式。
why: last quarter is a finished time in the past. The revenue passed the branches' total then, so use the simple past: surpassed.
last quarter 是已結束的過去時間。營收就是在那時超過分店總和，所以用過去式：surpassed。

gloss.ex: Revenue rose by ten percent this year.
Each retail branch opens at nine.
They redesigned the website last spring.

point: A clause with that left out: the verb is active.
省略 that 的子句：動詞用主動。
why: The subject of have been offered is The two interns. In between is a clause with that left out: the head of the payroll department assigned the interns. The head acts, so the verb is active: assigned.
have been offered 的主詞是 The two interns。中間是省略了 that 的子句：薪資部主管 assigned 了實習生。主管是做動作的人，所以用主動：assigned。

gloss.ex: Our intern helped with the spring survey.
The payroll department closes its books on Friday.
The company offers good benefits to all staff.

point: An opening participle shares the main subject: passive uses p.p.
句首分詞的主詞就是主句主詞：被動用 p.p.
why: The subject of the main clause is the tenants. They did not give the notice; they received only two days' notice. So the opening word is passive: Given.
主句的主詞是 the tenants。他們不是發出通知的人，而是收到 only two days' notice 的人。所以句首用被動：Given。

gloss.ex: We gave staff a week's notice.
The tenants pay rent on the first.
Please wash these glasses by hand.

point: A noun + Ving: the Ving phrase describes the noun.
名詞 + Ving：Ving 片語修飾前面的名詞。
why: The main verb is the distant should inform. Everything from Employees to October is the subject. Wishing describes Employees, like who wish.
主要動詞是遠處的 should inform。從 Employees 到 October 都是主詞。wishing 修飾 Employees，相當於 who wish。

gloss.ex: She asked to transfer to the Boston office.
Each department head approves leave requests.
Please confirm your request in writing.

point: Only a noun phrase follows: use a preposition.
後面只有名詞片語：用介系詞。
why: the revised safety regulations that the city council passed in March is only a noun phrase. Passed belongs to the that clause. There is no main verb before the comma, so the blank needs a preposition: In light of.
the revised safety regulations that the city council passed in March 只是名詞片語。passed 屬於 that 子句。逗號前沒有主要動詞，所以空格要介系詞：In light of。

gloss.ex: New regulations take effect next month.
Workers put up scaffolding around the building.
She is a certified public accountant.

point: Whether … or not means 'no matter if'.
Whether … or not 表示「不論是否」。
why: or not pairs with Whether. The firms will continue to share the center, no matter whether the merger is approved or not. The blank is Whether.
or not 和 Whether 成對。句子說的是：不論併購是否通過，兩家公司 will continue to share 物流中心。空格是 Whether。

gloss.ex: The merger created the largest bank in town.
Each shareholder received a copy of the report.
The distribution center ships orders every morning.

point: A, as well as B, + verb: agree with A.
A, as well as B, + 動詞：跟 A 一致。
why: Take out the part between the commas: as well as the two external auditors … accounts. The subject is The chief financial officer, which is singular, so the verb is is.
拿掉兩個逗號之間的 as well as the two external auditors … accounts。主詞是單數的 The chief financial officer，所以動詞用 is。

gloss.ex: The chief financial officer presented the budget.
The external auditor checks our accounts yearly.
The budget review starts at ten.

point: One of the + plural noun: the verb agrees with One.
One of the + 複數名詞：動詞跟 One 一致。
why: The subject is One. that deliver to our downtown branches only describes vans. One is singular, so the verb is has: has been out of service.
主詞是 One。that deliver to our downtown branches 只是修飾 vans。One 是單數，所以動詞用 has：has been out of service。

gloss.ex: The courier van leaves the depot at seven.
The bank has a downtown branch.
The copier is out of service today.

point: both of + relative word for people: whom.
both of + 指人的關係代名詞：whom。
why: The firm has hired already has its main verb. The clause have advised major retailers must describe two outside consultants. After of, the relative word for people is whom.
The firm has hired 已有主要動詞。have advised major retailers 這一句必須修飾 two outside consultants。of 後面指人的關係代名詞是 whom。

gloss.ex: We hired a consultant to review our costs.
Large retailers order goods in bulk.
The flagship store opens in May.

point: A complete clause with no missing object: use where.
子句完整、不缺受詞：用 where。
why: In the members of our regional sales team stayed during last year's conference, nothing is missing. Stayed takes no object. The clause tells the place, so use where, meaning at which.
the members of our regional sales team stayed during last year's conference 裡什麼都不缺。stayed 不接受詞。這個子句說明地點，所以用 where，意思是 at which。

gloss.ex: The regional sales team meets every Monday.
Groups get a reduced rate on weekdays.
Please book a table for six.

point: familiarize + reflexive pronoun + with.
familiarize + 反身代名詞 + with。
why: The doer of to familiarize is the sales associates. They are the ones who learn the policy, so the object is the same people: themselves.
to familiarize 的動作者是 the sales associates。要熟悉政策的就是他們自己，所以受詞用反身代名詞：themselves。

gloss.ex: Each sales associate wears a name badge.
Please familiarize yourself with the safety rules.
Our return policy allows refunds within thirty days.

point: Neither means 'not one of the two'.
neither 表示「兩者都不」。
why: The sentence ends with so it signed a lease on a third. So the company did not use either of the two buildings. Neither one had enough parking: neither.
句尾是 so it signed a lease on a third。所以公司沒有選那 two buildings 的任何一棟。兩棟都沒有 had enough parking：neither。

gloss.ex: The claims-processing team works on weekdays.
The lease runs for five years.
He works the evening shift on Fridays.

point: blame the result on the cause.
blame 結果 on 原因。
why: Blamed already has its object: the three-week delay. The cause comes next, the late arrival of steel beams, so the word before it is on.
blamed 已有受詞：the three-week delay。接著是原因 the late arrival of steel beams，所以前面用 on。

gloss.ex: Don't blame the driver for the traffic.
The east wing has a new lobby.
Steel beams hold up the roof.

point: prevent + person + from + Ving.
prevent + 人 + from + Ving。
why: The verb prevents comes before a long object: employees who have not yet completed the annual data protection training. After that object, prevent needs from: from opening.
動詞 prevents 後面接很長的受詞：employees who have not yet completed the annual data protection training。受詞之後，prevent 要配 from：from opening。

gloss.ex: Locks prevent thieves from entering the shop.
New data protection rules start in May.
Only managers can edit the client database.

point: consider + Ving.
consider 後面接 Ving。
why: The blank is the object of is considering. Take out among several other measures proposed by the finance department, and you get considering closing.
空格是 is considering 的受詞。拿掉插入的 among several other measures proposed by the finance department，就是 considering closing。

gloss.ex: We must cut costs this year.
The firm took new security measures.
My passport expires in May.

point: close to + Ving: this to is a preposition.
close to + Ving：這個 to 是介系詞。
why: The word closer sits far before the blank. Closer … to means near to something, and this to is a preposition. A preposition takes Ving: to signing.
closer 離空格很遠。closer … to 表示接近某事，這個 to 是介系詞。介系詞後面接 Ving：to signing。

gloss.ex: The stalled talks resumed on Monday.
The negotiation lasted three days.
The port facility handles large ships.

point: require that + subject + base verb.
require that + 主詞 + 原形動詞。
why: requires … that sets up a demand, so the verb after any shipment stays in the base form. The shipment gets invoiced, so it is passive: be invoiced.
requires … that 帶出要求，所以 any shipment 後面的動詞用原形。貨物是被開發票的一方，用被動：be invoiced。

gloss.ex: The contract has a clause on late payment.
The project is two weeks behind schedule.
The shipment arrived two days early.

point: Were + subject + to + verb: If left out.
Were + 主詞 + to V：省略 If 的倒裝。
why: The phrase to approve comes after the long subject the board, which has already postponed its decision twice this year. It fits if the board were to approve. Drop if and move Were to the front.
to approve 接在長主詞 the board, which has already postponed its decision twice this year 之後。這是 if the board were to approve 的句型。省略 if，把 Were 移到句首。

gloss.ex: They postponed the launch until June.
The manager must approve all expenses.
The expansion will add two new floors.

point: A comparison with than needs more.
有 than 的比較：用 more。
why: The sentence ends with than the two older branches nearby combined. That than makes this a comparison, so the blank needs the comparative: more customers.
句子後半是 than the two older branches nearby combined。這個 than 表示在比較，所以空格要比較級：more customers。

gloss.ex: The renovated lobby looks much larger.
On an average weekday we get fifty calls.
Combined sales reached two million dollars.

point: The number of + plural noun + singular verb.
the number of + 複數名詞 + 單數動詞。
why: The verb is the singular has nearly doubled. It describes the count of applicants, not the applicants themselves. So the subject is The number.
動詞是單數的 has nearly doubled。它說的是 applicants 的數量，不是應徵者本人。所以主詞用 The number。

gloss.ex: Every applicant must submit a résumé.
Sales doubled in two years.
The starting wage is twenty dollars an hour.

point: A list uses the same form for every item.
列舉的每一項用相同的形式。
why: include lists three items. The first two are ordering supplies and scheduling repairs, both Ving. The third must match: managing.
include 後面列出三項。前兩項 ordering supplies 和 scheduling repairs 都是 Ving。第三項要相同：managing。

gloss.ex: Please schedule the meeting for Friday.
The contractor finished the work on time.
Maintenance staff check the lifts weekly.
